newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Grains futures drop in high Budapest turnover.
newsitem.headline: Grains futures drop in high Budapest turnover.

text.p: Most grain futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) dropped on Friday, with dealers expecting the trend to continue next week.
"Although this week's drops would warrant a technical correction, that is unlikely to happen," said Robert Vajo of Termin Broker.
Maize futures finished 100 to 400 forints per tonne lower, with March closing at 18,200, off 300.
"There are actual physical deals behind most of the March contracts," Vajo said.
He added that ample maize and wheat surplus was behind this week's downward trend.
"There is plenty of wheat, plenty of maize and export hopes are thinner," he said.
Wheat prices registered a sharper downward movement, only restricted by the daily allowed maximum drop of 400 forints.
July milling wheat saw prices drop 350 forints to 21,250.
Turnover was high, especially considering the fact that the BCE only introduced Friday trading at the beginning of January and traders are taking their time to adjust.
Total turnover was 2,242 contracts or 902 million forints, of which maize accounted for 1,359 contracts and milling wheat for 633.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
